fields.description: The ERPNext user the read was performed for. Never Administrator, never a service account, never a shared login - an audit row naming a shared identity answers nothing.
fields.label: Accessed By

fields.description: Correlates this read with the Triton turn that caused it. For an Admin read it correlates the rows written by one viewer session.
fields.label: Request ID

fields.description: When the read happened, as recorded by the writer. This is the timestamp the chain signs - NOT `creation`. Frappe's Document.insert() calls set_user_and_timestamp() before anything else and assigns `creation = modified = now()` unconditionally for a new document, so a caller-supplied `creation` never survives; signing it meant signing a value the database never stored, and v1.268.0 reported its very first row as tampered because of it. This field is owned entirely by the writer and Frappe never touches it.
fields.label: Recorded At

fields.description: Why this read happened. Required for an Admin read and collected once per viewer session, not per scroll. For a Triton read it is the invocation id. Empty is legal only for a read that returned nothing.
fields.label: Reason

fields.description: What the SUBJECT is shown instead of the free-text reason (decision D-3). The free text is written for a compliance reviewer and can name a third party or an open investigation; this is the part an employee can be shown without the disclosure becoming the leak. NOT covered by chain_hash — adding a field to the chained tuple would re-hash every existing row and report the whole log as tampered. The authoritative, tamper-evident record is the free-text `reason`.
sha256 of the query text. The hash is stored by default and the text is not, because the query a manager types is itself sensitive.
fields.label: Query Hash

fields.description: Written ONLY when Chat Settings.store_retrieval_query_text is on, which ships off.
fields.label: Query Text

fields.description: One row per room the read touched, whether or not the reader was a member. Written always and marked per room: deciding participation per room and conditionally writing is more code and more ways to be wrong.
fields.label: Rooms

fields.description: sha256(previous row's chain_hash + canonical json of this row's audited fields). Makes silent tampering detectable, NOT impossible - anyone with database write access or root on the VM can rewrite rows and recompute the chain. Verify with erpnext_enhancements.chat.audit.verify_chain.
fields.label: Chain Hash
